about: The cases of oracle O8 (conformance/sdk/run.mjs) beside the spec's Style Examples table: the spec's own examples (Appendix C, the Parameter Object Examples) and the pitfalls the other generators' tests and changelogs show they fixed (map/research/codegen-2026-11/06-sdk-serialization.md). Each case is an operation (its parameters, requestBody, responses, path after /c<i>, method) generated in each of its versions (3.0.4, 3.1.2 and 3.2.1 when it names none); each call is a request input and what the request must hold (path, query, headers, body exactly; pairs and bodyPairs as WHATWG's form-urlencoded parser reads them), or a response (status, headers, and body, or bytes as hex for a body given as bytes) and what reading it gives (bytes: the body read back as exactly those bytes), or readsBytes, a content type and what flowapiReadsBytes says of it. A request's expected body is held to its UTF-8 when the request's is bytes, and bytes is the body as hex; an input's {"$bytes": hex} is bytes, {"$file": {bytes or text, name, type}} flowapiFile's, {"$blob": {bytes or text, as, blobType, name, type}} a Blob (a File named as) read by flowapiBlob, {"$unread": ...} a Blob given unread, {"$undefined": true} undefined; randoms are what crypto.getRandomValues gives in turn, and boundary: drawn puts the drawn boundary for {boundary}. targets names the SDKs a case is for when not every one can be given its calls (bytes that are not UTF-8: the Rust runner gives text). covers names the requirements each case is evidence for (the ledger reads them).
